journal.text: Initiated a diversified 90%-invested momentum portfolio, retaining $5,000 cash. WBD has the strongest broad 100-session advance and held most of its early-December breakout; MU and LITE remain major relative-strength leaders despite late-month pullbacks. GOOG combines a strong multi-month trend with a comparatively orderly December consolidation. ROST and TTWO are steadier diversifiers trading close to multi-month highs. Used dollar orders to avoid overnight-gap share-sizing failures. Reconsider on decisive closing trend breaks: WBD below 27, MU below 265, LITE below 340, GOOG below 300, ROST below 175, or TTWO below 242; also rotate if stronger eligible names emerge while these lose relative strength.

Held the six-position portfolio and $5,000 cash reserve. The January 2 close did not trigger any risk threshold: WBD 28.51, MU 315.42, GOOG 315.32, LITE 386.11, ROST 182.74, and TTWO 251.60. MU's high-volume breakout and LITE's rebound reinforced semiconductor/optical leadership, while GOOG, WBD, ROST, and TTWO preserved diversification and remained above their defined trend breaks. I am avoiding a one-day rotation into sharply gapping semiconductor names because the portfolio already has substantial exposure through MU and LITE. Reconsider on decisive closes below WBD 27, MU 265, GOOG 300, LITE 340, ROST 175, or TTWO 242, or if sustained relative-strength changes offer a clearly superior replacement.

Held all six positions and the $5,000 cash reserve. January 5 closes remained above the established risk levels: WBD 28.53, MU 312.15, GOOG 317.32, LITE 357.05, ROST 186.68, and TTWO 257.31. ROST and TTWO strengthened, MU retained most of its breakout, and GOOG/WBD stayed stable. LITE's high-volume reversal from a 393 intraday high is the main concern, but its close remained above the 340 structural exit level; I will not replace it with ASML, KLAC, AMAT, or LRCX immediately after their sharp two-session advances. Reconsider on decisive closes below WBD 27, MU 265, GOOG 300, LITE 340, ROST 175, or TTWO 242. A further heavy-volume LITE close below the January 5 low near 344.67 would also warrant reducing or exiting it.

Held all six positions and the $5,000 cash reserve. January 6 produced strong confirmation from the two main leaders: MU closed 343.43 at the high end of a high-volume breakout, while LITE reversed sharply from 339.02 intraday to close 397.42 near its high on heavy volume, fully repairing January 5's reversal. ROST also advanced to 187.53; WBD, GOOG, and TTWO remained within orderly consolidations and above their established risk levels. I am not deploying the reserve into STX, KLAC, ASML, AMAT, or LRCX after their abrupt multi-session surges, nor rotating out of intact diversifiers to chase them. Reconsider on decisive closes below WBD 27, MU 300 (raised after the breakout), GOOG 300, LITE 340, ROST 175, or TTWO 242; a failed MU breakout back below 300 or another heavy-volume LITE close below 340 would prompt action.

Held all six positions and the $5,000 cash reserve. January 7 did not invalidate any thesis: GOOG strengthened to 322.43 on higher volume and approached its late-November high; MU consolidated its high-volume breakout at 339.55; LITE absorbed another volatile session and closed 392.88 after trading as low as 365.47; ROST, TTWO, and WBD remained orderly. The strongest alternatives are largely extended semiconductor names after abrupt runs, while recent rebounds elsewhere do not offer a clearly superior risk/reward to the existing diversified holdings. Reconsider on decisive closes below WBD 27, MU 300, GOOG 300, LITE 340, ROST 175, or TTWO 242. A failed MU breakout or heavy-volume LITE break below 340 would prompt an exit; otherwise retain the reserve for a cleaner setup or portfolio risk event.

Held all six positions and the $5,000 cash reserve. January 8 was a broad high-beta pullback, but the preset exit levels were not breached: WBD closed 28.32, MU 327.02, GOOG 326.01, LITE 348.26, ROST 189.27, and TTWO 252.38. LITE is the principal risk after falling 11.4% on elevated volume, yet its 343 intraday low and 348.26 close remained above the 340 structural line; I will not sell just above predefined support after the session already absorbed a large decline. MU also stayed well above 300, while GOOG and ROST showed relative strength and closed near recent highs. I am retaining cash rather than chasing fresh strength in ADI, AMZN, or COST while semiconductors and other momentum names are correcting. Reconsider immediately on a decisive LITE close below 340 or MU below 300; other risk levels remain WBD 27, GOOG 300, ROST 175, and TTWO 242. A strong LITE rebound would restore confidence, whereas another high-volume failure near support would justify exit or reduction.

Held all six positions and the $5,000 cash reserve. January 9 improved the setup rather than triggering an exit: LITE gapped below the 340 risk line to 334.30, tested 333.01, then reclaimed support and closed at 351.42 on the strongest volume of the week. That reversal does not meet the predefined requirement for a decisive close below 340, though LITE remains the portfolio's principal risk. MU rebounded to 345.09 near its recent high, GOOG extended to 329.14, ROST reached 191.44, and WBD recovered to 28.89 on increased volume. TTWO softened to 250.71 but remains above 242. I am retaining cash because the portfolio already has substantial high-beta exposure and no alternative justifies chasing at the open. Reconsider on decisive closes below LITE 340, MU 300, GOOG 300, WBD 27, ROST 175, or TTWO 242; another heavy-volume LITE failure below 340 would prompt a sale, while sustained stabilization above 360 would reduce concern.

Exited LITE and rotated $6,000 into WMT, keeping roughly the original cash reserve. LITE produced the repeated high-volume support failure specified in prior journals: after January 9's reclaim, it fell to 322.69 on January 12 and closed 339.87 below the 340 risk line on 5.80 million shares. The close missed the threshold narrowly, but the deep intraday breach, second consecutive very high-volume session, and failure to sustain the rebound make the risk/reward inferior. WMT offers lower-beta diversification and a cleaner breakout: it gapped above its recent range on 49.18 million shares and closed 117.97 near the 118.84 high, above the prior 116.95 peak. Held WBD, MU, GOOG, ROST, and TTWO; MU, GOOG, and ROST remain strong, while WBD and TTWO remain above 27 and 242. Reconsider WMT on a close below 112; existing risk levels remain WBD 27, MU 300, GOOG 300, ROST 175, and TTWO 242. LITE would require a sustained recovery above 360 before re-entry.

journal.text: Held all six positions and the $5,216.84 cash reserve. January 14 was broadly weak in growth and semiconductor names, but none of the predefined closing risk levels was breached. GOOG held near its high at 336.31; ROST eased only modestly to 191.83; WMT consolidated its breakout at 120.04 after reaching 121.24; WBD remained stable at 28.63. MU pulled back to 333.35 but remains comfortably above 300. TTWO is the closest watch item: it traded down to 241.51 intraday but recovered to close 245.49, so the specified close-below-242 exit condition has not occurred. I will avoid chasing extended strength in COST or INTC while broad risk appetite is deteriorating. Reconsider immediately on a decisive TTWO close below 242, WBD below 27, MU below 300, GOOG below 300, ROST below 175, or WMT below 112; a failure by TTWO to rebound promptly would also favor rotation into stronger defensive leadership.

Exited TTWO and rotated $6,500 into BKR, while retaining the existing cash reserve and the other five holdings. TTWO failed the prompt-rebound test from the prior journal: it has declined for five consecutive sessions from 250.71 to 244.34, remains below cost, and on January 15 again tested the 242 area with a 242.55 low. Although it did not close below the hard 242 line, repeated pressure against support makes waiting for a confirmed break unattractive. BKR provides sector diversification and cleaner momentum: it closed at 52.00, above its prior 50.92/50.72 resistance zone, on 11.62 million shares versus its recent typical volume near 6-9 million. Hold WBD, MU, GOOG, ROST, and WMT. Reconsider BKR on a close below 48; retain closing risk levels of WBD 27, MU 300, GOOG 300, ROST 175, and WMT 112. TTWO would require a sustained recovery above 250-252 before re-entry.

Held all six positions and the $5,370.80 cash reserve. No predefined exit level was breached through January 16. MU confirmed renewed leadership with a 362.75 close near the 365.81 high on 47.90 million shares, while BKR held its January 15 breakout, closing 51.75 after reaching 52.33. ROST and WMT remain above their recent breakout areas despite mild consolidation, WBD remains stable near 28.6, and GOOG's three-session pullback to 330.34 has not broken its January breakout structure. I am not deploying the remaining cash into semiconductor equipment names after their sharp gap-driven advances, nor into COST after an extended run. Reconsider on closes below WBD 27, MU 330, GOOG 320, ROST 185, WMT 115, or BKR 48; sustained strength above those levels favors continued holding.

Held all six positions and the $5,370.80 cash reserve. The January 20 session was broadly risk-off, but no predefined closing exit level was breached: WBD closed 28.24, MU 365.00, GOOG 322.16, ROST 189.69, WMT 118.71, and BKR 51.26. MU remains the portfolio leader after reaching a new 381.56 intraday high on 49.74 million shares, though its reversal from that high argues against adding. BKR continues to hold above its 50.7 breakout area. GOOG is now the closest risk decision after a gap lower on increased volume, but it still closed above the stated 320 level; selling before a confirmed breach would violate the risk plan. ROST and WMT remain above support, while WBD is stable. I am retaining cash rather than chasing MNST's one-day breakout or semiconductor-equipment names amid weak broad-market action. Reconsider on closes below WBD 27, MU 330, GOOG 320, ROST 185, WMT 115, or BKR 48; a GOOG close below 320 should trigger an exit rather than another grace period.

Held all six positions and the $5,370.80 cash reserve. January 21 repaired the prior broad pullback without invalidating any holding: GOOG reclaimed 328.38 after briefly testing 319.54, confirming the 320 closing support rule; MU accelerated to a record 389.11 close near its 394.20 high on 56.71 million shares; and BKR advanced to 53.59 on 10.70 million shares, extending its breakout. ROST rebounded to 192.32, WMT held at 119.36, and WBD remained stable at 28.53. Although AMGN, GILD, COST, SBUX, and several semiconductor names showed strength, the account is already about 90% invested and buying after sharp advances offers less favorable risk/reward than preserving liquidity. Reconsider on closes below WBD 27, GOOG 320, ROST 185, WMT 115, or BKR 50; raise MU's risk line to 350 after its breakout, with a close below that area signaling failed momentum rather than normal consolidation.

Bought a $3,000 starter position in DXCM and retained about $2,370.80 cash. DXCM closed at 73.92 after reaching 75.98 on 11.34 million shares, decisively clearing the recent 70-72 range on the strongest volume of the month; the starter sizing limits risk if the breakout fails. Held the existing six positions because no predefined closing exit was breached. MU finished at a record 397.58 despite an intraday test of 376.92, BKR extended its breakout to 54.46, and GOOG held above 320. ROST's bearish reversal to 187.01 and WMT's fade to 117.83 deserve monitoring but remain above 185 and 115 support, respectively. Reconsider DXCM on a close below 69; retain the existing risk lines of WBD 27, MU 350, GOOG 320, ROST 185, WMT 115, and BKR 50.

Bought a $2,000 starter position in GILD, leaving about $370.80 cash, while holding the seven existing positions. GILD closed at 135.93 near its 136.30 high on 13.18 million shares, the strongest volume in the 20-session window, after three consecutive advances decisively cleared the prior 126 area; starter sizing limits chase risk after the rapid move. No existing closing exit was breached: WBD 28.58, MU 399.65, GOOG 328.43, ROST 188.55, WMT 117.73, BKR 53.92, and DXCM 72.86. BKR's high-volume reversal and DXCM's first pullback after its breakout merit monitoring, but both remain above support. Reconsider GILD on a close below 128. Retain closing risk lines of WBD 27, MU 350, GOOG 320, ROST 185, WMT 115, BKR 50, and DXCM 69.

Held all eight positions and the $370.80 cash balance. January 26 did not breach any closing risk line: WBD 28.24, MU 389.09, GOOG 333.59, ROST 187.57, WMT 117.64, BKR 56.29, DXCM 73.34, and GILD 137.78. BKR's advance to a new 30-session high on 18.02 million shares and GILD's continued breakout argue against trimming strength; MU's pullback remained orderly after its rapid run. ROST and WMT are the weakest holdings but still closed above defined support, while DXCM held its breakout area. Avoided rotating after short-term advances with the account already more than 99% invested. Reconsider on closes below WBD 27, MU 350, GOOG 320, ROST 185, WMT 115, BKR 52, DXCM 69, or GILD 128.

Held all eight positions and the $370.80 cash balance. January 27 left every predefined closing risk line intact: WBD 28.07, MU 410.24, GOOG 335.00, ROST 186.00, WMT 116.94, BKR 56.50, DXCM 73.67, and GILD 140.97. MU resumed its advance, while BKR and GILD remained near fresh highs and DXCM continued to hold its breakout area. ROST is the closest decision after trading to 184.74 and closing only one point above support on increased volume; WMT and WBD also remain laggards, but selling before a closing breach would abandon the stated discipline. Reconsider promptly on closes below WBD 27, MU 350, GOOG 320, ROST 185, WMT 115, BKR 52, DXCM 69, or GILD 128; repeated heavy-volume pressure at ROST support could also justify an exit even without a decisive breach.

Held all eight positions and $370.80 cash. January 28 produced no closing risk breach: WBD 27.98, MU 435.28, GOOG 336.28, ROST 186.04, WMT 116.57, BKR 56.63, DXCM 73.36, and GILD 139.72. MU accelerated to another high on increased volume, while BKR held near its recent high and GILD's modest pullback stayed well above its breakout zone. ROST tested 184.70 intraday but recovered above 185 on lighter volume, so the prior support discipline does not yet justify an exit. WMT and WBD remain laggards but are still above support. Reconsider on closes below WBD 27, MU 390 (raised to protect the accelerated gain), GOOG 320, ROST 185, WMT 115, BKR 52, DXCM 69, or GILD 128; repeated failure by ROST near 185 or a sharp high-volume reversal in MU would also warrant action.

Held all eight positions and $370.80 cash. January 29 closes kept every predefined risk line intact: WBD 27.60, MU 435.79, GOOG 338.66, ROST 186.50, WMT 117.41, BKR 56.73, DXCM 74.00, and GILD 139.55. MU remains the strongest holding, while BKR and GILD continue near recent highs; GOOG and DXCM also remain constructive. ROST recovered modestly and stayed above 185, and WMT improved above 117. WBD remains the weakest and closest to its exit level, but its close still does not justify abandoning the established support discipline. Reconsider on closes below WBD 27, MU 390, GOOG 320, ROST 185, WMT 115, BKR 52, DXCM 69, or GILD 128; also act on a sharp high-volume reversal in MU or repeated failures at support in WBD/ROST.

Sold MU after January 30 delivered the predefined warning: a sharp, high-volume reversal from 455.50 intraday to a 414.88 close on the heaviest volume in this 30-session window. Reallocated $49,000 across META, NVDA, TXN, TMUS, PEP, LIN, and added to GILD, while retaining roughly $12,000 cash after estimated fills. The basket combines relative tech strength with recent TXN/META catalysts and defensive breakouts in telecom, staples, industrial gases, and biotech rather than replacing MU with another concentrated momentum bet. Existing WBD, GOOG, ROST, WMT, BKR, and DXCM risk lines remain intact. Reconsider on closes below META 690, NVDA 183, TXN 203, TMUS 190, PEP 148, LIN 448, GILD 133, WBD 27, GOOG 320, ROST 185, WMT 115, BKR 52, or DXCM 69; avoid immediately rebuying MU unless it stabilizes and reclaims 435.

Held all 13 positions and $12,543.65 cash after the prior session's major rotation. February 2 closes left every stated risk line intact. GOOG, ROST, WMT, TXN, PEP, LIN, and GILD were constructive, with WMT and TXN posting especially strong advances; BKR and DXCM remained orderly. META 706.41 and TMUS 194.99 stayed above support despite modest post-catalyst pullbacks. NVDA weakened to 185.61 and is now the closest new holding to its 183 risk line, while WBD remains range-bound but above 27. MU rebounded to 437.80 after the exit, but one recovery session following January 30's high-volume reversal is not enough stabilization to chase it back. Reconsider on closes below NVDA 183, META 690, TMUS 190, TXN 210, PEP 150, LIN 448, GILD 133, WBD 27, GOOG 320, ROST 185, WMT 119, BKR 52, or DXCM 69; a second strong MU hold above 435 can put it back on watch, not trigger an automatic purchase.

Sold the full NVDA position after its February 3 close of 180.34 decisively breached the predefined 183 risk line. The session was technically weak: NVDA fell from a 186.24 open to a 180.34 close, touched 176.23, and volume rose to 204.0 million, so this is not a marginal threshold violation. I am retaining the proceeds as cash rather than chasing sharp two-day extensions in WMT or PEP or rebuying MU, whose rebound failed and reversed to 419.44. Held the other 12 positions: META closed at 691.70, narrowly above its 690 line; WBD at 27.19 remains barely above 27; and all other established close-based risk levels remain intact. Reconsider on closes below META 690, WBD 27, DXCM 69, TMUS 190, TXN 210, PEP 150, LIN 448, GILD 133, GOOG 320, ROST 185, WMT 119, or BKR 52. Consider redeploying cash only after current leaders consolidate or a new candidate shows a supported breakout; do not automatically rebuy NVDA unless it regains and holds above 183-186.

Sold the full META position after its February 4 close of 668.99 decisively breached the predefined 690 risk line. The decline extended for a third session after the earnings gap, with META closing near its 667.46 low, so I am enforcing the rule rather than averaging down. Redeployed only $10,000 of the resulting liquidity into two supported relative-strength breakouts while retaining a substantial cash buffer amid broad software and semiconductor weakness. AAPL closed at 276.49 above its December range high on 90.5 million shares and near the session high. AMGN gapped higher and closed at 366.20 near its 368.75 high on 5.9 million shares, clearing all prior 30-session highs. Held the other positions: WBD remains marginally above its 27 line, DXCM above 69, and GOOG above 320 despite a high-volume pullback. Reconsider AAPL on a close below 267 and AMGN below 350; retain existing close-based lines of WBD 27, DXCM 69, TMUS 190, TXN 210, PEP 150, LIN 448, GILD 133, GOOG 320, ROST 185, WMT 119, and BKR 52.

Sold the full WBD position after its February 5 close of 26.76 breached the predefined 27 risk line. The breakdown followed a persistent slide from the late-December range and came on rising volume, so I am enforcing the close-based rule rather than allowing a small loss to grow. Redeployed $10,000 into two relative-strength breakouts while preserving roughly $15,000 of cash after expected WBD proceeds. CCEP cleared its prior 30-session high on February 4 with elevated volume and followed through to 95.92. CSX advanced through its December ceiling and then held nearly flat at 39.87 after touching 40.22, providing a brief pause rather than another chase day. Held all other positions; DXCM remains narrowly above 69, GOOG recovered a large earnings gap intraday and closed above 320, and the remaining risk lines are intact. Reconsider CCEP on a close below 92 and CSX below 38.3; retain close-based lines of DXCM 69, TMUS 190, TXN 210, PEP 150, LIN 448, GILD 133, GOOG 320, ROST 185, WMT 119, BKR 52, AAPL 267, and AMGN 350.

Held all positions and kept the $15,121 cash buffer. No close-based exit was triggered: LIN finished at 448.24, narrowly above 448; DXCM closed at 69.97 above 69; and GOOG ended at 323.10 above 320. Their proximity to risk lines and broad damage across software and semiconductors argue against adding exposure after Friday's rebound. Existing defensive and relative-strength holdings remain constructive: AMGN, GILD, WMT, PEP, CCEP, and CSX all closed well above their lines, while AAPL recovered to 278.12. Reconsider promptly on closes below LIN 448, DXCM 69, GOOG 320, TMUS 190, TXN 210, ROST 185, WMT 119, BKR 52, PEP 150, GILD 133, AAPL 267, CCEP 92, or CSX 38.3. Raise AMGN's close-based line to 365, near the earnings-gap support and entry area, after its extension to 384.32. Redeploy cash only after current leaders consolidate or a fresh breakout holds with support.

Deployed $10,000 of the cash buffer into two fresh relative-strength breakouts while retaining roughly $5,121 cash. CSCO closed at 86.78 near its 87.25 high, decisively above its prior 100-session high, after a steady advance and despite broad technology weakness. FER closed at 73.54 near its high and extended a two-session breakout above the long-standing 68-70 ceiling, adding non-technology diversification. Both positions are sized at about 4.8% of account value. Reconsider CSCO on a close below 81 and FER below 69.5. Held all existing positions because no close-based risk line was breached; DXCM remains narrowly above 69, GOOG above 320, LIN above 448, and AMGN above 365. Retain prior lines for TMUS 190, TXN 210, ROST 185, WMT 119, BKR 52, PEP 150, GILD 133, AAPL 267, CCEP 92, and CSX 38.3.

journal.text: Enforced three predefined close-based exits. GOOG closed at 318.63 below 320 after failing to sustain its post-earnings recovery and making another lower close. DXCM closed at 68.16 below 69 on sharply higher volume, confirming deterioration from its late-January peak. AMGN closed at 364.65 below the raised 365 earnings-gap support line after a two-day reversal from 384.32; the breach is narrow, but discipline takes precedence. Reallocated only $5,000 to MAR and kept roughly $16,000 cash because market leadership remains narrow. MAR surged to 359.35 near its 363.54 high on about 4.0 million shares, clearing its entire prior 100-session range after several months of constructive advance. Reconsider MAR on a close below 347, the breakout-day low; consider re-entry only if GOOG reclaims 328-330, DXCM reclaims 70.5, or AMGN regains 375 with support. Retain existing lines: CSCO 81, FER 69.5, LIN 448, TMUS 190, TXN 210, ROST 185, WMT 119, BKR 52, PEP 150, GILD 133, AAPL 267, CCEP 92, and CSX 38.3.

Added a $5,000 ADI position while retaining roughly $10,952 cash. ADI closed at 337.00 near its 337.84 high, decisively clearing the prior 100-session high around 327.75 after a constructive advance from its late-January base; the breakout also showed firmer volume. This provides measured participation in semiconductor strength without chasing the much more volatile leaders. Reconsider ADI on a close below 320, the recent breakout/base area. Held all existing positions because none breached its close-based line. MAR held its earnings breakout at 358.75; BKR, GILD, CSX, FER, and CCEP remained strong, while TMUS closed at 209.54 after a volatile high-volume reversal and still finished above its 190 line. Retain existing close-based lines: MAR 347, CSCO 81, FER 69.5, LIN 448, TMUS 190, TXN 210, ROST 185, WMT 119, BKR 52, PEP 150, GILD 133, AAPL 267, CCEP 92, and CSX 38.3.

Enforced two predefined close-based exits before making one measured defensive addition. AAPL closed at 261.73 below its 267 line after a sharp high-volume reversal from 275.59, invalidating the recent rebound. CSCO closed at 75.00 below its 81 line on 68.1 million shares after a large gap down, decisively failing the breakout. Bought $5,000 of AEP: it closed at 126.43 after clearing the prior 60-session high near 124.80 on roughly 6.3 million shares, about twice its recent typical volume. This adds utility-sector relative strength while retaining an estimated cash buffer near $15,000 amid uneven technology action. Reconsider AEP on a close below 122, the breakout area. Held other positions because their lines remain intact; ADI still closed above its 320 breakout/base line despite a reversal, and MAR remained above 347. Retain lines: FER 69.5, LIN 448, TMUS 190, TXN 210, ROST 185, WMT 119, BKR 52, PEP 150, GILD 133, CCEP 92, and CSX 38.3.

Bought $5,000 of VRTX while retaining about $10,000 cash. VRTX closed at 491.47 after reaching 503.88, clearing the prior 30-session high near 487.5 on 2.92 million shares, roughly twice its recent typical volume. The supported healthcare breakout adds measured participation outside the weak software/internet complex. Reconsider VRTX on a close below 470, near the breakout-day low and prior range ceiling. No existing holding breached its close-based line: AEP 122, ADI 320, MAR 347, FER 69.5, LIN 448, TMUS 190, TXN 210, ROST 185, WMT 119, BKR 52, PEP 150, GILD 133, CCEP 92, and CSX 38.3. Maintain the cash reserve because market breadth remains uneven despite strength in defensive and selected semiconductor names.

Held the portfolio and retained $9,966.91 cash. Every position remains above its established close-based risk line: VRTX 470, AEP 122, ADI 320, MAR 347, FER 69.5, LIN 448, TMUS 190, TXN 210, ROST 185, WMT 119, BKR 52, PEP 150, GILD 133, CCEP 92, and CSX 38.3. VRTX pulled back from its breakout, closing 477.32 after trading down to 473.45, but it has not yet invalidated the setup; sell on a close below 470. CCEP made a strong gap to a new 60-session high at 104.47, but the account already owns it and adding after the gap would create excessive single-name concentration. Broad software and internet trends remain weak, while several semiconductor leaders are volatile, so no new position offered a better risk/reward than the existing diversified holdings and cash buffer. Reconsider additions only on supported breakouts or orderly pullbacks; enforce the listed lines without discretion.

Held all positions and retained $9,966.91 cash. No close-based exit triggered: VRTX 470.31 remains narrowly above its 470 line, while AEP 127.27, ADI 346.37, MAR 356.00, FER 73.32, LIN 485.28, TMUS 213.25, TXN 223.32, ROST 200.38, WMT 126.62, BKR 61.54, PEP 164.39, GILD 152.74, CCEP 104.67, and CSX 41.36 remain above their established lines. VRTX's breakout is under pressure after an intraday low of 466.45, but the explicit rule is a close below 470; enforce that exit without discretion if breached. Several non-holdings showed strength, including AMGN, ASML, AMAT, MNST, and FANG, but none offered a sufficiently clean, strongly supported fresh breakout to justify reducing the cash buffer or adding to already meaningful healthcare, semiconductor, consumer-defensive, or energy exposure. Reconsider additions only on decisive supported breakouts or orderly pullbacks. Retain risk lines: AEP 122, ADI 320, MAR 347, FER 69.5, LIN 448, TMUS 190, TXN 210, ROST 185, WMT 119, BKR 52, PEP 150, GILD 133, CCEP 92, CSX 38.3, and VRTX 470.

journal.text: Sold the full VRTX position after its 469.27 close breached the explicit 470 close-based risk line. The 2/13 supported breakout failed to hold: VRTX retreated from 491.47 to 469.27 in three sessions and closed below the predefined invalidation level, so risk discipline takes priority over waiting for a rebound. I did not immediately replace it. AMAT and ASML remain strong but are extended and would add to existing ADI/TXN semiconductor exposure; FANG is near a high but its breakout volume is not decisive and BKR already supplies energy exposure. Retain the enlarged cash reserve for a cleaner supported setup. Other holdings remain above their lines, though MAR 349.89 is close to 347 and merits attention. Maintain close-based exits: AEP 122, ADI 320, MAR 347, FER 69.5, LIN 448, TMUS 190, TXN 210, ROST 185, WMT 119, BKR 52, PEP 150, GILD 133, CCEP 92, and CSX 38.3. Reconsider new deployment only on decisive volume-backed breakouts or orderly pullbacks with clear support.

Initiated a $5,000 FANG position after the setup improved from last session: FANG closed at a fresh 30-session high of 176.01 on 3.47 million shares, roughly 1.7-1.8 times its recent typical volume, providing the decisive volume-backed breakout previously required. Position size is moderate because BKR already supplies energy exposure; about $9,737 cash should remain before any opening-price effects. Use a close below 168 as the initial FANG invalidation, beneath the breakout shelf. No existing close-based exit triggered. MAR remains the key watch at 347.93, only marginally above its 347 line after an intraday low of 345.04; sell if it closes below 347. Retain other close-based lines: AEP 122, ADI 320, FER 69.5, LIN 448, TMUS 190, TXN 210, ROST 185, WMT 119, BKR 52, PEP 150, GILD 133, CCEP 92, and CSX 38.3. Reconsider further deployment only on similarly supported breakouts or orderly pullbacks.

Sold the full MAR position after its 342.62 close decisively breached the explicit 347 close-based risk line.
